safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
(حتّى) is a particle of limit and of genitive.. and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن زرتم) is in the position of genitive through (حتّى), attached to (ألهاكم).
Clause: «ألهاكم التكاثر ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «زرتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(ألهاكم): it contains an i'lāl (weak-letter change) by substitution, treated like تلهّى.. see verse (10) of Sūrat ʿAbasa; the alif is written long because it falls in the middle of the word.
(زرتم): it contains an i'lāl by elision, in keeping with the construction on sukūn; the zāy takes a ḍamma to indicate that the original of the alif is a wāw; its wazn is فلتم.
(المقابر): plural of المقبرة, a noun of place from the triliteral قبر; its wazn is مفعلة with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn because the ʿayn of its imperfect takes ḍamma; and the tāʾ is for emphasis.

safi-cedvel:3-4.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is for rebuke and reproach. (سوف) is a particle of futurity. (ثمّ) is for conjunction. The object of (تعلمون) is omitted, its implied form being: the evil outcome of boasting.
Clause: «سوف تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «سوف تعلمون (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrīr): in His saying, the Exalted: «ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ».
It was repeated to reinforce the rebuke, and ثم indicates that the second is more eloquent, just as a great man says to his servant, "I tell you, then I tell you: do not do it." It was said: and because it is more eloquent it is treated as though it were different from the first.

safi-cedvel:5-8.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (علم) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (ترونّ) is an imperfect, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of similar letters; and (the wāw) is the fāʿil (agent) [Note: the wāw was not dropped on account of the dropping of the ʿayn of the verb.], and (the nūn) is the heavy nūn of emphasis..
Clause: «لو تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.. and the apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being: "you would not have busied yourselves with boasting" or "you would have turned back from disbelief".
And the clause: «ترونّ الجحيم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
7-8 (ثمّ) is a conjunction in both places. (لترونّها) is like the first. (عين) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar [Note: either because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "you will surely see it with a sight that is ʿayn al-yaqīn", or because it meets it in meaning, since "sight" and "witnessing" are one thing; and taking (عين) as a maṣdar involves some licence.], (لتسألنّ) is like لترونّ, with the pronoun of the agent dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters. (يومئذ) is an accusative – or indeclinable – adverb of time attached to (تسألنّ), and the tanwīn in (إذ) is a compensation for something omitted, i.e. "on the day when you see it". (عن النعيم) is attached to (تسألنّ).
And the clause: «ترونّها ... » is the response to another implied oath [Note: or it is conjoined to the preceding response clause.] ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the preceding oath clause.
And the clause: «تسألنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ترونّها.

* Morphology:
(6) ترونّ: the verb contains an i'lāl by elision: its lām – the yāʾ – was dropped, as was its ʿayn, the hamza.. Its original is لترأيون; the yāʾ, being vowelled after a fatḥa, turned into an alif; then the alif was dropped because it met the wāw as a sākin, giving لترأونها – with fatḥa on the hamza and sukūn on the wāw; then the vowel of the hamza was moved to the rāʾ before it; then the hamza was dropped for heaviness and because of the meeting of two sākins; then the nūn, the sign of the nominative, was dropped on the entry of the heavy nūn of emphasis and the coming together of three nūns; then the wāw was given a ḍamma because of the meeting of two sākins.. its wazn is تفونّ, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the fāʾ and ḍamma on the wāw.

* Rhetoric:
1- Omission (ḥadhf): in His saying, the Exalted: «لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ».
The apodosis of لو is omitted to inspire awe, i.e. if you knew thus, you would do what cannot be described or fathomed, or that would distract you from rivalry in multiplying and from other things.
2- Clarifying a thing after leaving it vague: in His saying, the Exalted: «لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ».
Here He made clear to them what He had warned them of and threatened them with, by way of magnification and exaltation; and the oath is to confirm the threat, and that what they were threatened with admits no room for doubt.
3- Repetition (takrīr): in His saying, the Exalted: «ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ».
Here He repeated the oath, joined by ثم, to harden the threat and increase the awe.

* Benefits:
- «لتسألن عن النعيم» ("You will surely be asked about the bounty"):
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The first thing a servant is asked about on the Day of Resurrection of the bounty is that it will be said to him: Did We not keep your body healthy for you, and give you cold water to drink?
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day or one night, and there were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. The Prophet ﷺ said: What has brought you out of your homes at this hour? They said: Hunger, O Messenger of Allah. He said: And I – by Him in whose hand is my soul – what brought me out is what brought you out. Rise! So they rose with him, and he came to a man of the Anṣār. When his wife saw him she said: Welcome! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: Where is so-and-so? She said: He has gone to fetch fresh water. Then the Anṣārī came, looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two companions, and said: Praise be to Allah, no one today has more honourable guests than I. He went off and brought them a bunch of dates containing unripe dates, ripe dates and fresh dates, and said: Eat. He took up the knife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Beware of the milch animal. So he slaughtered a sheep for them, and they ate meat and dates and drank. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about this bounty on the Day of Resurrection: hunger brought you out of your homes, and you did not return until this bounty reached you. Reported by al-Tirmidhī.
